internal/llmprompts is not internal/prompts, which is the P246 popup router.
registry.go in internal/llmprompts is the one file containing prompt text.
A llmprompts registry entry has id, kind, apps, title/purpose/usedBy catalog keys, applies-when, default, required fragments, and fixed output schema.
Typed handle Prompt[V] has Text(src, vars); NoVars is used for entries without variables.
Not in the llmprompts registry: user-authored text such as smart-script bodies and workflow stage and step prompts.
Not in the llmprompts registry: tool and server names, tool error strings, and result data formatting.
llmprompts entry kinds: system, message, suffix, instructions, tool, argument, toolResult, fragment.
Kind argument is one MCP tool property description and carries Parent tool and Field.
Kind fragment is included via {{template}}.
InputSchema[T] sets each MCP tool property's description from its argument registry entry.
A mismatch between InputSchema[T] and argument entries panics at server build.
jsonschema tags are not used.
llmprompts templates use text/template, one set per resolve, with funcs inc and join only.
An entry with NoVars and no fragments is literal and never parsed.
Default prompts render byte-identical to the pre-P271 output, checked against testdata/golden.
RenderParts wraps each string variable in marker runes and splits, so Settings Preview marks resolved values with VarText.
A failed self-check in RenderParts returns one literal part.
Prompt override store is <home>/llm-prompts.json per app: ~/.kira-studio/ and ~/.kira-space/.
The store file is written with renameio, mode 0600.
Store shape: {version, revision, overrides: {id: {text, defaultHash, updatedAt}}}.
Saving the default text removes the override.
Override text must be 1 byte to 32 KiB.
A prompt change carries baseHash; a stale change is refused with E_CONFLICT.
A corrupt store file, or an override that no longer validates, falls back to the default and logs a warning.
Settings flags corrupt store and invalid override as storeError and invalid.
defaultChanged flags an override made against an older default.
Server-side prompt validation checks the template parses and every prompt:"required" variable is referenced.
Server-side prompt validation checks every required fragment is included and the template executes against example vars.
Required fragment memory.dataHygiene (injection defence) is in the memory system prompts.
Schema-bound prompts (gate, reconcile, import extract and finalize) keep their JSON schema fixed, shown read-only in Settings.
There is no global prompt source.
Consumers get a llmprompts.Source (Resolve, Revision) through options: memory.ServiceOptions, mcpserver.Options, claudeheadless, scriptruns, ADE, dbmcp.
Defaults() is the registry-only source.
Store.Resolve stats the file per call and re-reads on mtime or size change.
Gate, reconcile, import, headless suffixes and ADE messages resolve per call, so an edit applies on the next call.
memory-mcp is a stdio subprocess; memorycli.Run gets <KiraSpaceHome>/llm-prompts.json.
memory-mcp builds server instructions, tool and argument descriptions once per process, so edits apply to new Claude sessions (newSession, shown in Settings).
dbmcp and claudeheadless rebuild their MCP server when Revision() changes.

Drafts live in Pinia store llmPromptDrafts; dialog Save saves prompts first, then the settings patch.
Guard go run ./internal/llmprompts/cmd/checkprompts is part of bun run lint.
checkprompts fails on a jsonschema tag.

stored.fact: Kira Studio is a native macOS workbench: a database client for ten engines plus an HTTP/gRPC API client.
Kira Studio is built on Wails (Go) and Vue 3.
Kira Studio has four modes: Studio (database), Api, Automations, Docker; one button switches between them.
Kira Space is a sibling app of Kira Studio in the same repo, at apps/kira-space.
Kira Space is a git client and code workspace with coding agents, memory store, terminal, and phone view on home network.
Kira Space docs are in apps/kira-space/README.md.
Kira Studio is beta; expect bugs and breaking changes between builds.
Kira Studio supports only macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon (arm64).
Kira Studio supports dark mode only.
Kira Studio builds are ad-hoc signed, not notarized.
Each new build counts as a different app to Keychain, so first launch after an update may prompt; choose Always Allow once per build.
Saved credentials are encrypted at rest in macOS Keychain.
Touch ID (or system password) is required before revealing a saved password.
Install with scripts/install.sh using --app=studio, or --app=space for Kira Space.
scripts/install.sh downloads the latest release disk image, moves the app to /Applications and opens it without a Gatekeeper prompt, unlike a browser-downloaded DMG.
The installed app checks GitHub for a newer release and offers an update.
There is deliberately no silent auto-update; nothing installs until the user clicks Update.
Build Kira Studio from source with `bun run package:studio`.
package:studio installs its own dependencies first: Bun workspace, Go module, pinned wails3 CLI.
Build output is apps/kira-studio/bin/Kira Studio.app and Kira Studio.dmg.
A locally built app needs a Gatekeeper workaround on first launch: right-click Open, or xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the app.
Kira Studio supports engines: PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MySQL (8.0.16+), SQLite, ClickHouse, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka, SQS, S3.
ClickHouse is insert only in Kira Studio.
Redis writes cover string keys; delete works on any type.
Kafka is produce only.
SQS supports send and delete.
S3 supports writes plus upload/download; other engines have full writes.
Query consoles: SQL engines use SQL, MongoDB uses shell-style, Redis uses commands.
Kafka, SQS and S3 have no query console.
Stop cancels the operation itself (pg_cancel_backend, KILL QUERY, cursor abort, consumer stop), not only its display.
SQS never polls on its own; it reads only when Poll is pressed.
SQS polling is manual because ReceiveMessage hides messages from real consumers.
Connections support fields or URI mode, and test-connection.
Each connection has a read-only guard enforced in the backend.
Connections support an optional pre-connect script, e.g. port-forward.
Connections can be imported from a JetBrains DataGrip project.
Credentials can be pasted into a connection; review recognised values before applying.
Update credentials on a saved connection changes only username and password.
The same table can open in many tabs, each with its own paging, sort, filter and scroll.
Session restore reopens tabs without auto-connecting.
Data grid is virtualized in both directions.
Data grid page sizes range from 10 to 10k, with count-all on request and column projection.
Data grid supports server-side WHERE/ORDER BY with history and saved filters, and in-page find.
SQL edits are staged as a pending change set with exact command preview; nothing reaches the database until commit.
Document, key/value and stream writes apply immediately.
Cell editor is Monaco.
Cell editor detects JSON, XML, SQL, base64, hex, epoch seconds/milliseconds, ISO-8601, CSV, with beautify and compact.
Foreign-key navigation works only for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite.
Foreign-key navigation previews the referenced row in a popover, opens it in a pre-filtered tab or edits directly.
Query console is per-connection with run-statement/run-all, saved queries and Format.
EXPLAIN works for every SQL dialect, with optional auto-explain flagging expensive queries.
SQL completions, diagnostics and hovers come from a DDL document the user pastes in.
Column masking (PII) has six masks with live preview and is display-only; data is never changed.
Generate data fills a SQL table with fake rows using per-column recipes inferred from types.
Kira Studio operations panel shows live operations with duration, rows, command, cancel and re-run.
Kira Studio keeps a persisted operation log.
Kira Studio caching is three-tier with no speculative prefetch (docs/PERF.md).
Kira Studio shortcut for new window is ⇧⌘N.
Kira Studio shortcut for command palette is ⇧⌘P.
Kira Studio Automations are scripts organized in collections.
Each automation script runs in its own folder under app home or a chosen folder.
Automations keep run history with status, exit code and result.
Automation scripts can recur on a cron schedule.
A due scheduled run asks confirmation by default and never replays a missed run.
Kira Studio smart script is a prompt run by headless Claude Code.
Smart script parameters are typed: text, select, multi-select, secret.
Smart script sets model, budget, timeout, and a tick list of allowed tools and MCP servers.
Kira Studio Docker mode manages a local engine or saved context.
Docker mode handles containers, images, volumes, networks, live logs and stats, and exec terminals.
A remote tcp:// Docker engine without TLS works but is flagged insecure.
Kira Studio Api request builder supports method, URL, params, headers and body, with a raw request editor alongside.
